title: Normalized comparison of constant scalar realization with an ordinary scalar tower
statement: Let (C,J) be a site with objects in universe u+1 and morphisms in universe u, R and T commutative rings in universe u+1, f:R→T, B a commutative ring sheaf, and σ and τ maps from the constant R and T sheaves to B. Assume the two scalar units agree on r and f(r), and the weak sheafification and locally bijective comparison hypotheses of [lem-sfb-scalar-dual-evaluation-descent]. Then, naturally for every R-module N, realization B⊗_R N is isomorphic to realization B⊗_T (T⊗_R N); the isomorphism sends each constant generator a⊗x to a⊗(1⊗x). No finite presentation or flatness is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), normalized scalar comparison; Stacks, Tags 03EK and 0GMW.

proof.text: Construct the forward map from constant generators a tensor x mapped to a tensor (1 tensor x). Compatibility of the scalar units proves balancing. For the inverse, the ordinary extension/restriction adjunction extends x mapped to 1 tensor x on each section; generator extensionality proves restriction naturality.

Use ordinary scalar-extension extensionality and constant-generator extensionality to prove both inverse identities. Calculate on constant generators to prove the required normalization and naturality in N. This is the previously proved GenericScalar block extracted unchanged from the parent item for the per-file compile limit.

mathlib_searches.query: A constant sheaf module realization followed by scalar extension preserves a matrix cokernel and its quotient projection, and an invertible change of rows identifies the cokernel with the remaining coordinates

Found ModuleCat.isColimitCokernelCofork and PreservesCokernel.iso with its projection equation. These are used to construct the normalized comparisons; neither supplies the coefficientwise finite-power normalization or the rank-tail computation.

The parent item already contains the complete generic GenericScalar scalarModel_spec proof. Extracted that proof verbatim into this module; no new mathematical argument, hypothesis or axiom is introduced. Read ModuleCat.ChangeOfRings adjunction and ScalarDualEvaluationDescent generator universal properties.
